jonathan ditmar.name: Jonathan Ditmar
jonathan ditmar.origin: Jonathan Ditmar was a scientist who was put in charge of a Peace Commission to meet aliens who had approached Earth. During the meeting, the aliens made it clear that they intended to colonize the Earth thanks to their superior technology and enslave its inhabitants unless in the short space of a week the Earthlings gave some reason not to be colonized. Speaking of which, Jonathan let out a whistle of surprise, but the ones who were really surprised were the aliens who didn't know music. Jonathan then offered the aliens to land on Earth where they could listen to more music created by Earthlings, which the aliens did and then left for their world loaded with music and musical instruments, with the decision not to invade Earth again until Earthlings would produce such music.

jonathan dozer.name: Jonathan Dozer
jonathan dozer.origin: In an alternate future curiously similar to that of Killraven, bionic simian aliens from Mars invaded an Earth devastated by nuclear war and subjugated the survivors of humanity with Tripod like war machines, using brainwashed human scientists known as the Generals to maintain order for them. A General named Raker, put in charge of training gladiators to fight for the Apes' amusement, secretly trained a young boy named Jonathan Dozer to be his weapon against the invaders. Escaping before his training was complete after defeating the ape named Warlord, Dozer became Apeslayer, leader of a band of Freemen dedicated to overthrowing the invaders. Six years later, Apeslayer repaid Raker's faith in him by killing him, unaware that Raker had been planning to free him all along anyway. The dying Raker revealed Dozer's past history to him, and told him he had powers which would help him defeat the apes, but unfortunately perished before he could tell him what they were. Apeslayer faced Warlord again, but ultimately let him go after defeating him in battle. It is unknown whether Apeslayer and his band ever succeeded in overthrowing the Apes.

abilities: Superior combatant
weapons: Various swords, knives and blasters

jonathan east.name: Jonathan East
jonathan east.origin: When Jonathan East discovered that he had the power to project his will onto other people, he became the world's greatest expert on ESP. He conducted many experiments and travelled the world in search of opportunities to refine his abilities. He returned to the US, where he constructed a machine called the "Psycho-Intensifier". He fought Spider-Man by attacking him mentally, as well as through the use of the Synthetic Man, an android into whom East could project his consciousness. He was defeated when the Psycho-Intensifier magnified the ringing of East's doorbell enough to destroy his brain.

jonathan franklin murdock.name: Jonathan Franklin Murdock
jonathan franklin murdock.species: Child of a human mutate, later depowered
jonathan franklin murdock.origin: Jackie Murdock was the son of Matt Murdock, the vigilante known as Daredevil and mayor of San Francisco, who had been born apparently without a trace of his father's super powers. Shortly after Jackie's birth, Matt retired from his super hero career. When Jackie was fourteen months old, the inherited hypersenses abruptly appeared, and he was tormented by them. He would bruise at the merest touch and the simple scent of his mother's perfume would make his nose bleed. With the help of Dr. Valeria Richards, Jackie was cured six months later, and his hypersenses were suppressed. But he suffered from permanent psychological scars which would make him jump at the weakest sensitive stimuli if taken by surprise. Jackie later devoted to studying, and his father tried to make him exercise to be more active and social. When he was 9 years old, and in the day before Matt's fiftieth birthday, Jack was part of the seventy-two percent of the population of San Francisco who lost their sight due to a strange phenomenon. This was a result of Jackie being one of the numerous inhabitants of the city who used cyber-optic eye-drops. His father discovered the responsible for this and managed to bring back the sight of those who had lost it, including Jackie, but at the cost of his super human abilities. Back at his house, Jackie was helping Matt prepare their dog for a trial run as a guide dog. Matt offered Jack to join him in the walk, but he refused as he was scared for the wreckage there still was. As Matt and his dog were about to cross the street, a police car was approaching, which none of them noticed. Jackie quickly pushed Matt out of the way. As they were standing up, Jackie asked his father if he was going to be okay, for which he replied they both were.

jonathan gallagher.name: Jonathan Gallagher
jonathan gallagher.origin: ===Early Life=== Johnathan Gallagher was the son of Jack Beckley of the United States Air Force. John's grandparents were enraged when Jack went out to the South Pacific as a naval aviator; Jack was unaware that his fiancee was pregnant. Her family sent her to Florida to have the baby, who was then put up for adoption. Returning as a highly decorated hero; Jack married his fiancee and they had two children, Stephen and Rosemary. Jack remained unaware of the existence of his older son, John. John eventually became a powerful figure in naval intelligence and developed his own top secret intelligence agency known as The Bridge. As the leader of the organisation, John was known as the Superior. Tracing his own background, John discovered the identity of his father. John went to see Colonel Jack Beckley and told him he was his son. Jack, however, not knowing the truth, said he had only one son. The vengeful John determined to destroy the Beckley name and arranged an airplane crash in which Colonel Beckley died.

jonathan gatesworth.name: Jonathan Gatesworth
jonathan gatesworth.origin: Jonathan Gatesworth was a videogame developer and founder of SoftSCAPE, specialized in virtual reality; for SoftSCAPE he created the console Compuboot and the game Killer Teenage Aliens from the Mutant Death Star. He was eventually kicked out of his company by his collaborators, Marc Portaccio and Larson Toddsmith, who ultimated and published Gatesworth's latest work, Killer Teenage Aliens - The Even Bigger Adventure, without him. Wanting revenge on his former partners, he built a suit capable of projecting illusions using Compuboot's technology and called himself Netshape. Netshape attacked the Killer Teenage Aliens unveiling, intending to destroy Compuboot and Portaccio and Toddsmith's fortune (after having already attacked them at a videogame convention), but was stopped by Green Goblin. Impressed by Netshape's technology, SoftSCAPE's competitors offered themselves to pay for Gatesworth's legal defense in exchange for the virtual reality suit's rights, much to Toddsmith's dismay.

jonathan josten.name: Jonathan Josten
jonathan josten.origin: Jonathan Josten was the father of Erik Josten, later known as the super-criminal Power Man, Goliath and subsequently the Thunderbolt Atlas. Following Erik’s rise to infamy as a notorious superhuman criminal, the Josten family name fell into disgrace within their local community. Jonathan and his wife Martha were increasingly shunned by neighbors and business associates, and local institutions refused to extend them credit. The loss of trust and financial support led to the rapid decline of their livelihood, culminating in the loss of their farm. Shortly thereafter, Jonathan Josten died, followed soon by the death of his wife. Erik Josten would only learn of his parents’ deaths much later, at a time when he had begun seeking redemption and attempting to reform as a member of the Thunderbolts. Erik Josten's grave was close to his wife Martha, their younger daughter Lindy, and their older son Carl. 200px|left

jonathan lee.name: Jonathan Lee
jonathan lee.first_appearance: Silver Sable and the Wild Pack Vol 1 2
jonathan lee.origin: Jonathan Lee had been a criminal accountant experienced in laundering but ended up in prison. Silver Sable, impressed by Lee's talent, got him out of prison so that he could work for her, foiling other people's laundering. Lee also worked as a consultant for Silver Sable International, coordinating the expenses of Sable's mercenary operations. Due to the enormous value of his services, he was paid very generously by Sable, more than most of her employees and freelancers including Paladin. Lee often protested against the loss-making missions that Sable took, and presented bureaucratic complaints that Sable actively chose to ignore. Lee operated out of both Sable's base, Castle Sable, in Symkaria, and the Symkarian Embassy in New York City, headquarters for operations on American soil; Lee had some responsibility for the security systems at the Embassy. thumb|left|Mr. Lee (far right) insists on discussing the balance. Lee objected to hiring violent bounty hunter Karl "Crippler" Striklan, although Sable's manager, Mortimer, was already accustomed to Lee disapproving every such decision. Shortly after, the Embassy suffered an attack by the far-right group Watchdogs, and Sable decided to talk to Lee because the Embassy's security system had been insufficient. Not long afterward, Lee attempted to protest to Sable because she had hired Paladin for a mission in South America that had not yielded direct profit, and to those costs was added damage caused by the Wild Pack in Castle Doom, Latveria, whose owner insisted that Sable pay. Menacingly, Lee proposed cutting top salaries (which did not worry Paladin, since he was freelancing and other employers were willing to pay his price). Lorna Kleinfeldt, Sable's personnel manager, physically shook Lee and ordered him to make the accounts balance, or she would "cut Lee's pay" (said in such a way that it could have been a metaphor). In fact, Lee did reduce Paladin's wages. Even so, Lee stuck to his accountant guns and, when Sable decided to leave Castle Sable on a mission to stop the criminal organization Genesis Coalition could use the Cyberwarriors as a weapon, Lee protested that no one was paying them for that mission. Once again, Sable stepped over Lee. The Foreigner, a crime lord enemy (and occasional ally) of Sable, sought a controlling interest in Silver Sable International. The Foreigner used Lee, possibly under duress, to make Lee embezzle millions of dollars from Sable, a considerable amount of the company's capital gains that put them in trouble. An associate of Lee in this operation was money launderer Maurice Grauline. The Foreigner paid Lee for his service, as well as taking other action against Sable. Lee then fled with the money. As soon as Mortimer found out, he informed Sable, and she sent Paladin to track down Lee in an operation that would last weeks. Paladin began working with a technician at the Symkarian Embassy, discovering details about Lee on the computers. During that time, Sable's lover Jacques Girard learned of Lee's crime and took pity on Sable. Meanwhile, Paladin found Grauline in Canada and, under threat, Grauline told Paladin where Lee was. After beating up more people, Paladin finally found Lee and apprehended him at Plaza Hotel, New York City. Paladin hung Lee from a flagpole thirty stories up and threatened to hurt Lee's crotch if he didn't tell him where the money was. Lee framed the Foreigner, explaining his plans. fields.history: Jonathan Lee had been a criminal accountant experienced in laundering but ended up in prison. Silver Sable, impressed by Lee's talent, got him out of prison so that he could work for her, foiling other people's laundering. Lee also worked as a consultant for Silver Sable International, coordinating the expenses of Sable's mercenary operations. Due to the enormous value of his services, he was paid very generously by Sable, more than most of her employees and freelancers including Paladin. Lee often protested against the loss-making missions that Sable took, and presented bureaucratic complaints that Sable actively chose to ignore. Lee operated out of both Sable's base, Castle Sable, in Symkaria, and the Symkarian Embassy in New York City, headquarters for operations on American soil; Lee had some responsibility for the security systems at the Embassy. thumb|left|Mr. Lee (far right) insists on discussing the balance. Lee objected to hiring violent bounty hunter Karl "Crippler" Striklan, although Sable's manager, Mortimer, was already accustomed to Lee disapproving every such decision. Shortly after, the Embassy suffered an attack by the far-right group Watchdogs, and Sable decided to talk to Lee because the Embassy's security system had been insufficient. Not long afterward, Lee attempted to protest to Sable because she had hired Paladin for a mission in South America that had not yielded direct profit, and to those costs was added damage caused by the Wild Pack in Castle Doom, Latveria, whose owner insisted that Sable pay. Menacingly, Lee proposed cutting top salaries (which did not worry Paladin, since he was freelancing and other employers were willing to pay his price). Lorna Kleinfeldt, Sable's personnel manager, physically shook Lee and ordered him to make the accounts balance, or she would "cut Lee's pay" (said in such a way that it could have been a metaphor). In fact, Lee did reduce Paladin's wages. Even so, Lee stuck to his accountant guns and, when Sable decided to leave Castle Sable on a mission to stop the criminal organization Genesis Coalition could use the Cyberwarriors as a weapon, Lee protested that no one was paying them for that mission. Once again, Sable stepped over Lee. The Foreigner, a crime lord enemy (and occasional ally) of Sable, sought a controlling interest in Silver Sable International. The Foreigner used Lee, possibly under duress, to make Lee embezzle millions of dollars from Sable, a considerable amount of the company's capital gains that put them in trouble. An associate of Lee in this operation was money launderer Maurice Grauline. The Foreigner paid Lee for his service, as well as taking other action against Sable. Lee then fled with the money. As soon as Mortimer found out, he informed Sable, and she sent Paladin to track down Lee in an operation that would last weeks. Paladin began working with a technician at the Symkarian Embassy, discovering details about Lee on the computers. During that time, Sable's lover Jacques Girard learned of Lee's crime and took pity on Sable. Meanwhile, Paladin found Grauline in Canada and, under threat, Grauline told Paladin where Lee was. After beating up more people, Paladin finally found Lee and apprehended him at Plaza Hotel, New York City. Paladin hung Lee from a flagpole thirty stories up and threatened to hurt Lee's crotch if he didn't tell him where the money was. Lee framed the Foreigner, explaining his plans. Possibly after this, Lee went to prison, and perhaps the Foreigner attempted to assassinate him. In any case, Silver Sable International's financial matters were considered solved soon after that.

jonathan logan.name: Jonathan Logan
jonathan logan.origin: A former enemy of Dazzler back in her disco days, Johnny was never really a successful super-villain. Although he did constantly attempt to make it big with his partner and best friend, Doctor Sax, they never succeeded in realizing their goals. Later on, during the events of Dark Reign, when Norman Osborn decided to try and retake the inter-dimensional prison 42, Johnny was recruited along with Doctor Sax to be a part of the Shadow Initiative that would lead a first assault on the prison. However, Johnny arrived early for a team briefing, and overheard Taskmaster and Constrictor discussing how weak the Shadow Initiative was and how its only purpose was to die while softening up the target. Sickened, Johnny returned to his room, and decided that he has always been a failure. However, he decides to leave a better life for his daughter and wife, and makes sure that they will be generously compensated by the government in the event of his death. He is killed during the assault on 42, but only dies after saving the life of Doctor Sax. His last thoughts are of his daughter, and that she can know that he died serving his country, for her.
abilities: Jonathan Logan was a professional-level lead guitarist.
weapons: Guitar capable of firing sonic blasts

jonathan mcfee.name: Jonathan McFee
jonathan mcfee.origin: The population of Almost Reno, New Mexico, were rendered sterile by atomic tests. In an effort to control mutantkind, Odysseus Indigo's Damocles Foundation approached them, and offered to return their ability to have children. The Damocles Foundation injected the townspeople with both mutant and deviant DNA, which restored their fertility and ensured that any of their children would be born superhuman, and thus ideal test subjects for Indigo. One of these children was Jonathan McFee, who had the ability to generate fire with a snap of his fingers. He was a friend of the girl called Mary, and it was to her he first revealed his powers. Unfortunately, his powers destabilized the next day, and he was consumed by them. His death prompted X-Force to investigate the town and the Foundation.

weaknesses: Like most of the Deviant/mutant hybrid he suffered from unstable genetics.

jonathan pangborn.name: Jonathan Pangborn
jonathan pangborn.origin: Jonathan Pangborn was working in a factory setting when he suffered an industrial accident that left him with a crippling spinal injury. Confined to a wheelchair, he soon suffered through more misadventure when he began experiencing pain in his shoulder, but despite the efforts of health professionals there was little that could be done for his ailing body. Pangborn eventually decided that if he couldn't elevate the state of his body he would try to elevate his mind, and so he sought out a succession of gurus and holy men before finally finding a teacher in a Nepalese sanctuary known as Kamar-Taj. In Kamar-Taj, Pangborn learned how to channel extradimensional energy, and used that knowledge to rebuild his body. There was much more he could have learned there, but he was content with merely regaining the full use of his body, and so he returned to his old life back in the United States. Some time later he was approached by Dr. Stephen Strange, a brilliant surgeon who Pangborn had once unsuccessfully approached for treatment and who was now suffering from a crippling injury of his own. Pangborn took pity on the man and told him of Kamar-Taj before parting company. A long time afterwards, Pangborn was approached by an old acquaintance from Kamar-Taj, Karl Mordo, who spoke to him at length about the true purpose of magic. Mordo's intensity quickly put Pangborn on edge and had him reaching for his workshop tools for something to defend himself with, and his fear proved to be justified when Mordo attacked and overpowered him. Mordo then stripped him of his power, and without the energy to sustain himself, Pangborn collapsed back into the crippled state that had marred his life before.
abilities: Metalworking: Jonathan Pangborn is an experienced metalworker with years of factory engineering experience.
weaknesses: Energy Dependency: Jonathan Pangborn requires mystical control over exadimensional energy to remain able-bodied. Once stripped of his power he reverts to a physically crippled state.

jonathan rich.name: Jonathan Rich
jonathan rich.origin: The assistant of US Senator Andrew Jackson Hawk, Jon Rich was also an undercover agent of the Mandarin in a mission to destroy Tony Stark's credibility so that the United States of America stopped using Stark's defense technology and fall prey to Mandarin's attack from behind the Iron Curtain, starting WWIII. However, Hawk suspected that someone was planting evidence against Stark and secretly called Stark to stage a trap for the traitor. When Rich stole a briefcase from Stark and intended to use it as a proof, the proof exploded and Hawk revealed his plan. The Mandarin, monitoring it all, killed Rich while the police was arresting him.

jonathan rickman.name: Jonathan Rickman
jonathan rickman.origin: Jonathan Rickman was a scientist present at the accident that turned Otto Octavius into Doctor Octopus, during which he lost an eye but other emerged unscathed. A colleague, Christina Carr, however, was horribly scarred. Eventually, learning she also acquired the ability to transform into a super-powered male form, "Captain Power", she began systematically killing the other survivors. Rickman realized what was happening but was attacked by Christina before he could act upon this knowledge. His apartment was set on fire, and although Spider-Man rescued him, he later died of his injuries. Rickman did live long enough to tell Peter Parker when he visited him in the hospital.

jonathan standish.name: Jonathan Standish
jonathan standish.origin: Jonathan Standish was an extremely devoted Purifier who, during the events of Fear Itself, thought the end of the world was upon all humans. Standish believed all super-people were responsible for the end, so he kidnapped and later killed one on a live, online broadcast. Standish then pleaded for all humans watching to not give demons their souls, and to kill themselves to reach heaven. He then began sending other Purifiers to commit suicide attacks to kill as many as possible in the twisted belief that he was sending them to Heaven. X-Force tracked him down and learn that he was about to unleash an EMP weapon that would shut down every mind within a 25-mile radius. X-Force managed to take out the plane he was flying and prevent him from activating the weapon. Wolverine then finished Standish by decapitating him.

jonathan storm clone.name: Jonathan Storm (Clone)
jonathan storm clone.origin: Judged by his fellow Watchers for his constant interference in the lives of the people of Earth, Uatu was forced to train a young watched named Aron on the Watchers code of non-interference. However, after an interaction with the Fantastic Four, Aron became obsessed with not just observing, but controlling the events of those he watched. Developing a suit of armor that rendered him invisible to Uatu's gaze and procuring the android Dragon Man, Aron sought to obtain the DNA samples of the Fantastic Four. With the help of the Frightful Four, Aron succeeded in his task. He then created clones of the existing members of the Fantastic Four, Mister Fantastic, the Invisible Woman, the Human Torch, the Thing, and Ms. Marvel. With the real Fantastic Four put in suspended animation so he could watch their dreams, Aron sent the clones out into the world to take their place. Their first order of business was to recreate the first battle against the Fantastic Four's oldest foe, the Mole Man. Raising the previously sunken Monster Isle from the ocean floor, the cloned Fantastic Four attacked the Mole Man and his minions. After defeating their foes, the clones fled the island after setting off a massive explosion. Seeking to recreate the Fantastic Four's encounter with the Miracle Man, the clones later attacked an innocent magician during a stage performance and exposed how he performed his magic tricks to an increasingly hostile crowd. Feeling under appreciated for their "efforts", the clone of Mister Fantastic suggested that they begin charging a "Fantasti-Tax" in order to pay for their services. Eventually the activities of the clones attracted the attention of the Avengers and Doctor Strange who came to believe that some outside force had changed the real Fantastic Four's personalities. However before the fight could get out of hand, the clones all found themselves teleported back to Aron's hideout in the Rocky Mountains. There they discovered that the Fantastic Four and Frightful Four had broken free and were battling it out, while Aron himself was trapped in suspended animation. The Fantastic Four and their clones battled it out with one another until the real Fantastic Four defeated them. Freeing himself from suspended animation, Aron came to the conclusion that experiencing the dreams of others was more fascinating than their real life exploits, he sent the Frightful Four to the Vault, the real Fantastic Four home, and spirited off to manipulate the dreams of his clones. Although Aron has appeared since, there has been no word on the final fate of his clones.
powers: On par with the real Human Torch

jonathan torgson.name: Jonathan Torgson
jonathan torgson.origin: thumb|left|127px|Jonathan Torgson Jonathan Torgson was born with a number of deformities that led to him being shunned and mocked by the people of Pocano County, Pennsylvania. From his secluded home, Torgson became mad and decided to get revenge against those who mocked him. To this end, he built a massive exo-skeleton that enhanced his strength and fashioned it to look like a massive headless body. In the summer of 1943, he then began terrorizing the region, causing acts of sabotage and murder, earning him the name the "Headless Monster" in the newspaper. His reign of terror attracted the attention of Captain America and Bucky who went to investigate. Torgson attacked the two heroes and then fled into a nearby cave where he doffed his exo-skeleton and posed as on of the Headless Monster's hapless victims. Finding Torgson in the cave shouting for help, Captain America and Bucky escorted him back home unaware that he was really the Headless Monster. Later, Torgson issued a challenge to Captain America demanding that he meet him at the Playground amusement park. Captain America and Bucky answered the challenge and chased the Headless Monster and lost him in the Tunnel of Love. Fleeing back to his home, Torgson had a local paperboy find Captain America and Bucky and tell them that he feared that the Headless Monster was going to attack him in his home. As expected, the two heroes rushed to Torgson's home where he allowed them to find a secret passage way to a cavern that had a pit filled with water. As the Headless Monster, Torgson pushed them into the pit, but the two heroes managed to climb up. Rushing the Headless Monster, Captain America stripped the exo-suit off Jonathan. Torgson then explained why he created his alter ego, and then managed to break away from the hero and then climbed up onto a high up ledge. Before Captain America and Bucky could stop Torgson, he then threw himself off the ledge and fell to his death.

jonathan tremont.name: Jonathan Tremont
jonathan tremont.origin: In a village in the foothills of the Himalayas in rural India, there were three brothers: the eldest was wise, the second was strong, and the third was charming. Their abilities were derived from exposure to a shard of Triad energy that crashed in the mountains. However, a disease swept the town, killing the two older brother but sparing the youngest. The youngest brother preserved his brothers' souls by housing their spiritual energy inside him as they passed. He vowed to make something of himself. When the youngest brother was older, Hal Chandler came through the village looking for the shard in the mountains. In the 1950s Chandler had been the superhero "3-D Man", empowered by a second Triad shard. The youngest brother was hired on with him as a guide, but when he found what Chandler was looking for, the youngest brother struck Chandler and took the shard. The youngest brother grew stronger having found the shard, giving him the ability to summon the ghosts of his two brothers as avatars of chaos and order. It also showed him a vision of an impending threat known as the Triple-Evil. Changing his name to Jonathan Tremont, the youngest brother moved to the United States and founded the Triune Understanding. He held Chandler captive as he tried to harness the power of Chandler's shard for himself. Unable to do so, Tremont decided to find a new bearer for Chandler's powers. He found one in the man who would become known as Triathlon. Tremont's efforts to draw new converts to the Triune Understanding led him to target the Avengers. Using Pagan and Lord Templar to maneuver the Avengers, Tremont launched a media campaign to discredit the Avengers. He later "redeemed" them by forcing the team to accept Triathlon as a member. When the Triple-Evil came to attack Earth, Tremont went into space with the Avengers. He was captured by the Avengers after he tried to steal the Triple-Power from Triathlon, but when they were distracted by the arrival of Kang, he sacrificed his life, grabbing temporary control of the Triple-Power to charge Kang's force fields.

jonathan ware.name: Jonathan Ware
jonathan ware.origin: Jonathan Ware was a librarian who in 1946 decided to take up a life of crime, developing the costumed identity of Mother Goose. With his assistant King Cole they robbed the very library he worked at, taking Emerson first editions and leaving behind a clue to his next crime in a nursery rhyme. The Human Torch and Toro were called in to help solve the case. However, Mother Goose managed to best them when stealing the "Goose Woman" painting from the Fine Arts Museum. His next crime was to steal the three "Pepper Rubies" from Mrs. Kronite. However the Torch and Toro interfered with this theft as well, and Mother Goose only made off with two of the rubies. In order to get the third one, Mother Goose kidnapped Mrs. Kronite's son and held him for ransom, demanding the Torch deliver the ruby at a nearby preservation forest. After the exchange, Mother Goose managed to lose the Torch in the woods thanks to a photograph set up with an imitation of Toro crying for help. Changing back into his civilian identity, Ware showed up with Toro to offer his assistance, dropping the next clue in on of his own foot prints. When the Torch realized the clue was no dirty he correctly deduced that Ware was Mother Goose, but Ware fled the scene. When the two heroes tracked him down to his home, Ware unleashed his trained cats on them forcing the heroes to fall through a trap floor and knocked them out. He then put the two heroes in air tight asbestos suits and suspended them in the room that was rigged to an explosive set off by electronic beams. The villain then left the Torch and Toro to die while he and King Cole robbed the Watch Palace. However, the Torch and Toro escaped from the death trap and easily rounded up Mother Goose and King Cole, turning them over to the police. Ware's subsequent fate is unknown.
weapons: As Mother Goose, Ware relied on his wits and used objects around him to his advantage. At his home he trained his two cats to attack people on command.

jonathon gittes.name: Jonathon Gittes
jonathon gittes.first_appearance: Captain America/Nick Fury: Blood Truce Vol 1 1
jonathon gittes.origin: An agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. At the end of the Cold War, Gittes was involved in a conspiracy of S.H.I.E.L.D. agents who opposed to Communist war criminals escaping trial and punishment by deserting. He convinced fellow agent Nate Thurman to join their fiels as Thurman's brother CIA field officer George Thurman had been killed by KGB torturer Dmitri Panshin, and sent imbecile armored agent Agent Orange to try and kidnap Panshin in Euro Disney when the latter tried to defect to the US government. Agent Oranged failed, partly because the Titanium Man tried to "rescue" Panshin to hire him for A.I.M. During tha toperation, S.H.I.E.L.D. Helicarrier security boss "Dum Dum" Dugan was injured and replaced by Thurman; S.H.I.E.L.D. also involved Captain America in the operation to protect Panshin. Gittes made a new attempt, sending Agent Orange to kidnap Panshin in Prague, but failed due to the Titanium Man and Captain America. Agent Orange however managed to kidnap Panshin's young son Sergei Panshin, which Gittes used as a bargaining chip to have Panshin delivered, while pretending that Hydra was behind the operation; by having access to S.H.I.E.L.D.'s receiving comm technology, Gittes could pretend that Agent Orange was using a Hydra channel for contact. Thurman disliked the idea of endangering children, as this made them no better than Panshin; but Gittes insistently reminded Thurman of his dead brother. Agent Orange swapped Sergei for Panshin, then took Panshin to the Helicarrier. Thurman sealed the vehicle and Gittes arrested Dugan. Gittes then presided a kangaroo court on Panshin. However, Agent Orange had been followed by Captain America, the Titanium Man and S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Nick Fury; Gittes had expected only Fury to appear, so that he could convince the other agents he was an LMD impersonator. Agent Orange was defeated and Captain America found Panshin's cell, but Gittes confronted him with three other conspirator agents, including Goldman and Thurman, and intended to shoot Captain America dead if needed. Goldman refused to shoot Captain America himeslf, then when Gittes unsheathed his gun, Thurman punched and arrested Gittes, sick of how Gittes had used his brother's death for his own purposes.

jong.name: Jong
jong.origin: Colonel Jong was the liaison officer between his government and a former member of the Weapon Plus program named Butler. The North Koreans hired him to take prisoners from Jong's camp and transform them into super weapons against Korea's enemies. With captives in his custody, Jong and Butler used splices of mutant DNA from members of the X-Men and the mercenary Deadpool. These samples mutated the prisoners which gave them similar physical and ability characteristics to that of the X-Men. But after breaking free with the help of Deadpool, Wolverine and Captain America, they came together to defeat Butler and Jong died during the battle, stabbed by Deadpool.

jonothon cayre.name: Jonothon Cayre
jonothon cayre.origin: While working in America, Jonothon Cayre saw the Air Walker, Herald of Galactus, fighting Thor. When Thor destroyed it, he recovered a small piece of the robot, recognizing its self-regenerative abilities, and allowed the fragment to grow so that he could harvest its power, and build his own Air-Walker. Acquiring an L.M.D, Norm, in America, he returned to Scotland and began by creating a prototype Air-Walker which failed, and he abandoned it in a vault beneath his house. His second robot was much more successful, closely matching the original Air Walker, and able to wield the Power Cosmic. He then tried to use the self regenerating technology on himself, but it rejected him, constantly killing and resurrecting him, but giving him the power to control his molecular structure and unravel DNA. Driven mad, he destroyed the village of Carrin's Hollow in Scotland, by unravelling the DNA of the inhabitants. He then unleashed his plan, releasing the Air Walker to destroy, as well as his L.M.D Norm, who he armed with a nuclear bomb. He himself went to a pub, where the patrons hid him out of fear. Later, the Phoenix arrived and, with the patrons being unhelpful, she washed them away by opening all the kegs of beer in the pub, until they point out Dr Cayre. He had mutated into a new creature, the result of his failed experimenting on himself. He released a fluid from his hands, that unraveled the DNA of everyone left in the room except Phoenix, who shielded herself. He began to work his way through her shield, until she slammed a pool table on top of him. He oozed out from underneath, and tried to leave, knowing that they couldn’t kill each other. As Phoenix stepped on a glass shard, she had an idea. She trapped him in a glass prison that was taken to W.H.O. so they could attempt to cure him.
powers: Ability to control his molecular structure and .
abilities: Knowledge in science
weaknesses: His constant resurrections drove Cayre insane.

jonz rickard.name: Jonz Rickard
jonz rickard.origin: Jonz Rickard is the descendant of both Rick Jones and Emperor Rickard (the ruler of the First Terran Empire). He led the Galactic Avenger Battalion Theta-4 and guided the conquest of the Elan. He was also responsible for the slaughter of Centauri-IV, announcing this as punishment for a small rebellion. When the Avengers were brought to his reality and were captured by the Galactic Avengers Battalion, Rickard foiled Hawkeye's escape attempt by using his control of the Destiny Force. Rickard, believing the Avengers to be heretics for using what he thought was a duplicate of Captain America's legendary shield, fitted them with inhibitor collars and threw them into a cell for them to await execution. Fortunately, the Avengers were freed by Yellowjacket, who was temporarily allied with Immortus and were led back to Limbo. Rickard was later summoned with countless other Avengers from alternate realities by the Time-Keepers to stop Kang the Conqueror and the Avengers. The Time-Keepers were eventually defeated, and Rickard was presumably sent back to his native reality.
powers: Rickard has the power to control the Destiny Force.

joost van straaten.name: Joost van Straaten
joost van straaten.origin: Captain Joost Van Straaten was the captain of a ship that lusted only for treasure and was consumed with greed. He had no compassion for life, only wealth. He forced his crew into a storm to find treasure and the ship was overtaken by the raging sea. He and all his crew perished. When they met with Death, his crew's souls were allowed to rest but he was not. He was named the Flying Dutchman and sent to Limbo. The Flying Dutchman's Ghost was summoned by Mephisto and promised freedom from limbo if he destroyed the Silver Surfer. Warped by Mephisto's dark magic, the Flying Dutchman's Ghost was now stronger and had better weaponry, after pursuing the Silver Surfer through the city, they eventually met and battled, the Silver Surfer prevailed due to the Flying Dutchman's Ghost betraying Mephisto, The Silver Surfer shed a tear for the tortured and trapped soul of the Flying Dutchman's Ghost, and in turn, he was released from the bondage of Limbo.

joras kyl.name: Joras-Kyl
joras kyl.species: Kree given the powers of the Cipher during a White Event
joras kyl.origin: Joras-Kyl was a Kree scientist working at the Oceanica Science Station Pama-16 when Kree-Pama experienced a White Event. The phenomenon changed Joras-Kyl into Kree-Pama's new Cipher. After coming in contact with Nightmask, the two of them decided to look for the other heralds. . They next transported to the Temple of Pama where they found the third herald, Trrunk, who was transformed into Justice. After the three were together, they returned to New Kree-Lar to search for Va-Sohn, Mar-sohn's sister, who was the candidate to become the Kree Starbrand after Kree-Pama's Last White Event. As they found her, the White Event started, and, due to the absence of a Spitfire, the entity which would provide a counterforce to Starbrand's powers, the first thing she did with her newly acquired powers was to kill her brother Trrunk, stating that all she needed was the intelligence Cipher could provide. Stating that the best defence is a good offence, and knowing that Tarnax VII was the base for Super-Skrulls' training camps, Va-Sohn destroyed the entire planet. After doing so, Joras-Kyl and she were teleported to Starbrand's Structure by Libra so that both she and the Kevin would fight. However, they're unable to fight, as a fail-safe in the Starbrand power causes them to become attracted to one another and kiss. Because of this, they call off the fight and Va-Sohn agrees not to attack any more worlds, as Kevin would be there to "make things cosmically awkward". Therefore, Joras-Kyl and Va-sohn are returned to their homeworld to reconsider their options.

jordan gastin.name: Jordan Gastin
jordan gastin.origin: ===Deadly Regenesis=== Jordan Gastin was a mixed martial arts fighter whose fighting career was sometimes funded by their brother Drew’s criminal activities. During one of these heists, Drew was killed by Laura Kinney, at the time working as an assassin for Kimura and the Kingpin; for this reason, Jordan swore to avenge Drew. After Drew's death, Jordan's career stalled until Kimura, who they did not know was the Kinney’s former principal, found them and hired them. She had Gastin injected with MGH, after which Gastin started fighting again and earning Kimura's boss lots of money. Kimura, knowing the deep hatred Gastin harbored for X-23, having found her, asked them if they wanted to capture her: they happily accepted to bring her in. Equipped with some smoke grenades capable of temporarily neutralizing her powers, Gastin, now calling themselves Haymaker, got on a helicopter and went after her. They confronted Kinney and won the fight, being able to knock her out, shove her in the trunk of a car, and bring her to Kimura. Laura was forced to work for Kimura again. Understanding the rage Jordan was feeling, she visited them at the gym, trying to convince them about Kimura's malicious intent, but Jordan, even knowing X-23 was forced to kill their brother, still resented the young mutant and didn't believe her. After seeing how Laura refused to kill innocent people during a mission and how Kimura shot one of her guards just to make the girl mad, Haymaker started changing their mind. Kimura then brought the two to the Kingpin himself: he, disappointed in Kimura and her pupils, commanded for Jordan and Laura to be put in a cage. The two succeeded in escaping and, while Laura defeated Kimura, Jordan freed the prisoners of the facility. Laura tried to catch Kingpin's helicopter while he was escaping, but failed and fell from a building: luckily, Jordan was there to help her, having finally forgiven her. Two days later, Laura showed Jordan a mutual aid group to help them finally heal from the loss of Drew. ===Oasis=== Years later, Jordan started dating a mutant woman named Polly, who was directing Oasis, a refuge for mutants in New York, funded by money that Jordan was stealing from criminals. After some of the robbed criminals (now powered by MGH too) retaliated against the two, Laura Kinney, now called Wolverine, came to their help. Together, they raided an MGH laboratory, terminating the menace of the gang that was attacking them. Jordan showed up in Louisiana to help the X-Men put out a fire that was destroying a pediatric center and save the children trapped inside of it.
abilities: As an MMA fighter, Gastin has excellent martial arts and fighting skills.

jordan harrison.name: Jordan Harrison
jordan harrison.origin: Jordan Harrison was a Midtown High School student who helped his teacher Spider-Man in a fight against Doctor Octopus. He was later kidnapped by Calvin Zabo who planned to mutate him with a formula which would grant him powers similar to Spider-Man at the risk of eventually degenerating into a spider monster. With help from Spider-Man he was able to escape. Believing that Zabo had killed his mother, he threw a flask full of acid at his abductor's face, which Spider-Man tried unsuccessfully to stop, and returned to his mother.

jorge santiago.name: Jorge Santiago
jorge santiago.origin: Jorge Santiago was a mutant living in a village on the coast of Santo Marco, alongside his brother, Acero, and around thirty other mutants, including children and the elderly. After the fall of President Duarte, Jorge helped keep a portion of the coast relatively calm, in contrast of the chaos engulfing the rest of the country, notably by protecting the inhabitants from zoo animals which had escaped when Duarte had bombed the capital. He intervened in such a way as to knock out two polar bears heading for a reporter. When Jorge asked him not to write about his powers due to the anti-mutant sentiment that remained strong in his country, the reporter revealed his true nature as a killer cyborg sent by Weapon X. Jorge put up a good fight but was eventually killed by the assassin after ninety three seconds. His death was investigated by Logan, Sabretooth, Domino, and Warpath afterwards. Warpath gave his phone number to Jorge's brother Acero in case he ever needed help.
abilities: No confirmed intelligence rating was issued, and Jorge was consequently considered as C-Level.

jorro.name: Jorro
jorro.origin: Jorro was one of the Deviants of Lemuria and weapons-maker for his peers. He worked, apparently alone, in a huge underground laboratory/workshop, a few miles under the Earth's surface. Many Deviants, including Jorro, hated the Celestials, powerful cosmic beings who had created the Deviant race but also almost obliterated the Deviants when the later race had taken over the world and dared attacking their creators. left|thumb|Jorro in his lab, visited by Terminus Jorro's lab was eventually visited by Terminus, a 150-foot-tall monster who had been created by the world-conquering Terminex species when the Celestials decided to destroy the Terminex world and race; the Terminex intended for their legacy to be another species of world destroyers, and indeed Terminus had ravaged a number of planets before trying his luck on Earth. There, Earth champion Reed Richards of the Fantastic Four separed Terminus from his main weapon, the lance, and used an inertia-cancelling device to pummel him to the center of the Earth. While the pressure and intense heat of the molten level were not enough to kill Terminus, the lance was his propulsion source, and he had been forced to manually dig to the surface with his hands. Him finding Jorro's laboratory had been sheer chance, but Jorro and Terminus became natural allies as they both hated the Celestials with passion. Terminus then convinced Jorro to build and wear a replica of Terminus' space armor, then go to the surface world on a twofold mission: confront the champions of Earth so that Terminus would assess their power and not be unprepared as he had been with Richards, and recover Terminus's lance. Terminus's lance, admittedly huge but not useful in an obvious way, was being transported northway by boat from the Gulf of Mexico as a part of "Operation: Big Stick", a top-secret activity requiring all-clearance-holding crewmen. Detecting the lance, Jorro activated the weapon and summoned it to him near the Antarctica. Jorro, as Terminus, appeared from a huge whirlwind in the sea and broke the boat with his hands, killing all onboard except for a very injured single survivor. Security agency SHIELD discovered the shipwreck and asked the Avengers to investigate. At that point, the Avengers priority clearance had been temporarily suspended, without them being notified, and the American government was reluctant to give the Avengers information about the boat, the operation or Terminus himself; they were also unable to contact the Fantastic Four for information. Wielding the power of Terminus while wearing his armor, and working on his behalf, Jorro went to the Savage Land, a tropical preserve hidden in Antarctica, to obtain or destroy very advanced technology, including Celestial devices, hidden there. En route, Jorro stepped on a scientific research station, demolishing it. The Avengers tracked Jorro there, and followed him to the Savage Land. Terminus found a scientific team researching the Savage Land and guided by adventurer Ka-Zar, Lord of the Savage Land, causing a dinosaur stampede in the process. Seeing the humans trying to escape from him, Terminus decided to kill them as an entertainment, although Ka-Zar survived and was later found by the Avengers. After finding a Celestial instrument, Jorro detected more technology southward and, en route there, destroyed Ka-Zar's tree-based home, almost hurting Ka-Zar's wife Shanna the She-Devil - but she was rescued by flying Avenger Starfox, although Terminus slapped Starfox for interfering and stunned him. Following his sensors, Terminus reached Pangea, a huge selvatic environment, inhabited by primitive tribes and heated by volcanoes that were kept active by alien Nuwali environmental control machinery - the items detected by Jorro's sensors. Jorro found the primitive settlement Lemura and destroyed it, without having a real reason to do so except that he was angry because his search was taking too long; he then destroyed the Aerie Shalan, inhabited by the winged humans Aerians. In both cases, he killed all of the inhabitants. In the process, he also caused the Gorahn Sea to boil, destroyed the village of the primitive Fall People use the lace to destroy the Nuwali environmental control machines and unleashed earthquakes that damaged the Nuwali machinery beyond repair, thus causing the Antarctica inclement weather to immediately reclaim the territory. The inhabitants of Pangea were decimated, but the extradimensional woman M'Rin noticed their distress and, using her huge steed C'Jime, rescued a number of locals by taking them to her home dimension. Unaware of this, Ka-Zar and Shanna devoted the last minutes to rescue as many tribespeople as they could. thumb|left|Jorro's Terminus armor is damaged, the internal machinery shown The Avengers flew their Quinjet jet to confront Terminus, and Avenger leader Wasp identified Terminus' lance as a threat that should be removed. Another Avenger, the Black Knight, jumped from the jet attacking
weapons: Energy Lance: Terminus' original lance allowed Jorro to shoot beams that could kill people and destroy trees and rocks - but apparently with enough accuracy so as to not damage items he may be looking for in the area.

fields.personality: Jorro, like most Deviants, hated the Celestials but admitted that their technology was very advanced and coveted it for his own ends. While impersonating Terminus, Jorro behaved intimidatingly, treating human-sized people as worthless. While he did call them gnats and slapped flying vehicles and people, he was indeed sadistic and enjoyed the widespread destruction of population and cities. When physically hurt, Jorro was incredulous and far more insecure than the real Terminus was in combat, as he counted exclusively on the power of his technology, not on his own skill while using it. Once exposed, Jorro claimed to be the real Terminus, even when he could hardly win anything by doing so; he may believe that he was the real Terminus.

fields.notes: Marvel Pets Handbook (in the profile on Zabu) describes Jorro as a Deviant wearing Terminus' armor. However, both and say that Jorro was wearing a replica of Terminus' armor.

jose abejaron.name: Jose Abejaron
jose abejaron.origin: Jose Abejaron was the chauffeur for Merzah the Mystic. In his only recorded appearance, he drove Merzah and his assistant Diana Lanford to meet the challenge of Japanese spy Satokata Matsu. When Merzah and Diana were captured and taken to another location, Merzah used his telepathic powers to contact Jose, providing him with the address of where they were taken through a special screen in Jose's car that would display Merzah's thoughts as words. Jose attempted to rescue his employer and his assistant, but he accidentally knocked over a vase, alerting Matsu and his men of their presence. When Matsu attempted to flee the fight, Jose drove after them with Merzah in the passenger seat. Jose's driving skills allowed them to get close enough for Merzah to shoot out Matsu's tires, causing him to have a fatal car crash, ending his threat.
abilities: Jose was a skilled chauffeur and fighter.

jose comienza.name: Jose Comienza
jose comienza.origin: José Comienza and his wife Jema were two government agents in Cuba. Fidel Castro requested the help of the Red Room Academy, due to the suspicion the Comienzas were among the several who wished to defect with information to the United States. When Red Room operative Natasha Romanova was sent to infiltrate Cuba under the guise of being a Russian businesswoman that could help them, the Comienzas initially claimed to be in good graces with the government. In order to make them reconsider their relationship with the Americans, with whom the Comienzas had talked, Natasha planted miniature US flag in their front door to send them the message that somebody was watching. Jema convinced José to contact the Americans and flee as soon as possible, for the sake of their son Emiliano. However, when José was going to meet up with them, Natasha had wired their car and made it explode in front of José's eyes. In despair, José and Jema contacted Natasha to ask her to help them. When Natasha told them they'd need to give something in exchange, José gave her value information he possessed. With the potential intel the Americans could have wanted discovered, Natasha was ordered to dispose of José and Jema. The Comienzas were lured to Plaza Vieja, still thinking they were going to be given an opportunity to escape, and while they were waiting for their supposed transport, Natasha sniped them down. Starting with Jema, and then José.

jose fernandez.name: Jose Fernandez
jose fernandez.origin: Don Jose Fernandez was a penniless young man in fifteenth-century Seville; he fell in love, and was loved by Dolores, the daughter of Count Sebastian De Cazon, who opposed their love because he could not allow his daughter to marry a poor man and had therefore already given her in marriage to another. Leaving Seville, Jose ran to the aid of an old man who had fallen into quicksand and to thank him, the old man gave him a mystical ring that made the wishes of those who wore it come true. Although he did not believe this at first, Jose had to change his mind when, wishing for a new sword, a sword of pure gold appeared in his hands. Running to the castle to reclaim Dolores, thanks to the ring, he realized as soon as he arrived that he had lost the ring. Dolores was the daughter of the Spanish nobleman Count Sebastian De Cazon, in love with the penniless young Don Cose Fernandez whose love her father opposed because the young man was poor and had already promised his daughter in marriage to another person.

josef ansell.origin: Josef Ansell was the head of the Friends of New Germany, which strongly supports Nazi Germany and its Aryan racist ideology. Ansell created the Crime Master in abducting African-American minorities for Otto Octavius' experiments in using them to make mindless slaves. However, Ansell feared that Octavius' experiment would be exposed to the public due to the Crime Master's reputation being investigated by the federal authorities and the vigilante, the Spider-Man. Ultimately, Ansell decided to have Octavius' lab destroyed and all the prisoners killed. In extension, Ansell ordered Octavius to kill the Crime Master for being a liability to his organization.

josef huber.name: Josef Huber
josef huber.origin: Joseph Huber came from a wealthy family and was a powerful telepath (among other things) who claimed that the thoughts of all the mutants in the world were driving him crazy. He had used his family's wealth to hide himself away from the world and try to cope with his powers. He was first seen in the shadows meeting with Sasha Ryan. After M-Day, the voices he heard grew quieter as the mutant population was severely diminished and he sought to eradicate mutants altogether. To achieve this he manipulated and arranged all of X-Factor Investigations problems and adventures, including the X-Cell, Singularity Investigations, and the affair with the Purity Singers. He somehow arranged for a young French girl named Nicole (actually an android created by Huber) to be taken in by M and Siryn in Paris, seemingly of their own free will. This despite later stating that M and Siryn are immune to his telepathic suggestions. He convinced Jamie Madrox, Cyclops, and Beast to organize a "Million Mutant March" political rally to get mutants declared an endangered species by the United States government. However, Layla Miller told Madrox that one of Huber's agents had tried to kill her, and it was revealed that Huber's plan was a plot to get all the mutants in one place so they could be destroyed. Then he teleported the team to a frozen wasteland. Huber had teleported them to Antarctic where they were then out of communication range of M and Siryn, who were busy on a case, which had also been arranged by Huber, with the aid of a family of mutant haters. M became worried and flew back to X-Factor Investigations Headquarters, arriving just in time to stop Huber from smashing Rictor with a car, who had been more or less successfully fighting Huber. He was immune to the direct applications of Huber's mutant powers because Rictor was using Terrigen Crystals he had left over from his time with Quicksilver. fields.history: Joseph Huber came from a wealthy family and was a powerful telepath (among other things) who claimed that the thoughts of all the mutants in the world were driving him crazy. He had used his family's wealth to hide himself away from the world and try to cope with his powers. He was first seen in the shadows meeting with Sasha Ryan. After M-Day, the voices he heard grew quieter as the mutant population was severely diminished and he sought to eradicate mutants altogether. To achieve this he manipulated and arranged all of X-Factor Investigations problems and adventures, including the X-Cell, Singularity Investigations, and the affair with the Purity Singers. He somehow arranged for a young French girl named Nicole (actually an android created by Huber) to be taken in by M and Siryn in Paris, seemingly of their own free will. This despite later stating that M and Siryn are immune to his telepathic suggestions. He convinced Jamie Madrox, Cyclops, and Beast to organize a "Million Mutant March" political rally to get mutants declared an endangered species by the United States government. However, Layla Miller told Madrox that one of Huber's agents had tried to kill her, and it was revealed that Huber's plan was a plot to get all the mutants in one place so they could be destroyed. Then he teleported the team to a frozen wasteland. Huber had teleported them to Antarctic where they were then out of communication range of M and Siryn, who were busy on a case, which had also been arranged by Huber, with the aid of a family of mutant haters. M became worried and flew back to X-Factor Investigations Headquarters, arriving just in time to stop Huber from smashing Rictor with a car, who had been more or less successfully fighting Huber. He was immune to the direct applications of Huber's mutant powers because Rictor was using Terrigen Crystals he had left over from his time with Quicksilver. Huber turned to sand and floated away, disdaining tedious fighting in favor his planned genocide. He returned to his icy cave. Sometime later, the demoness Jezebel came to him, to propose a new genocide plan.
weaknesses: He has a mental block preventing him from directly killing mutants. Being close to another telepath creates mental feedback, causing him pain. He also requires medication to control his powers.
equipment: Telepathy-suppressing drugs, access to tremendously advanced technological devices of his own design.
fields.notes: In an interview, Peter David (Isolationist's creator) said that he was not a mutant, but failed to say how, exactly, he got his powers.
fields.trivia: Using Forge's powers Huber built "chaotic randomizing generator". He put it into Nicole's body so what then she was close to Layla Miller it allegedly thwarted her short-term precognition and made Huber and his agents invisible to Layla. However, with the latter revelation about true source of Layla Miller's "precognitions" it is unclear how exactly Huber managed to evade her knowledge.

josef saint.name: Josef Saint
josef saint.origin: Josef Saint was an elderly tailor living in Los Angeles. One day he stayed late working in his shop and was on his way home when he was attacked by a group of young hoodlums who beat him up. Saint woke up in the hospital, heavily injured and his entire face, minus his right eye, bandaged. Wallowing in futile rage, his latent ability manifested, and he found he could fire a paralyzing blast from his right eye. For months, he planned to start a vigilante activity against young criminals, or young people in general, in revenge for the attack, and also to sew his victims' lips together, apparently out of an exhibitionist tendency on his part. When Saint was released from the hospital six months later, he found that his tailoring business had closed, but he no longer cared; he only needed to keep the premises locked as a secret base of operations. He sewed together a costume and attacked young men on the city streets using his paralyzing powers and a large needle as his personal weapon, sewing their mouths shut with smaller needles afterwards. The newspaper reported the attacks, dubbing the attacker the Needle. This career began only a week after his release from the hospital, during which time he attracted the attention of S.H.I.E.L.D. agent Jerry Hunt, who was out on the street at the time and heard the screams of a long-haired boy being attacked. Hunt drew his weapon to confront the attacker, but the Needle paralyzed him with her hypnotic powers and decided that although Hunt was not one of "them" (the Needle's intended targets), Hunt had to pay for interfering: the Needle sewed up Hunt's mouth and fled. Hunt was sent to the hospital, and his girlfriend Jessica Drew (the up-and-coming superheroine Spider-Woman) decided to investigate and track down the Needle, against Hunt's advice, who found him too dangerous for her. The following night, the Needle attacked young Chuck, allowing his girlfriend Paula to flee; Spider-Woman found Paula and then a mouth-sewn Chuck, but the Needle had already fled, satisfied after a night in which he had attacked at least four men. When Hunt was discharged from the hospital later that day, Hunt and Spider-Woman collaborated on patrol together in search of the Needle, and Hunt found the Needle; Hunt fired at the vigilante, missed, allowing the Needle to paralyze him. Spider-Woman came to his rescue, firing a venom blast at Needle, which he dodged with extraordinary agility. A second blast hit and knocked Needle down; Spider-Woman went to disarm the Needle, but Needle was only pretending to be unconscious: His own power was so similar to Spider-Woman's venom blast that he was nearly immune to it, and so he had waited until she was within reach to grab her with his extraordinary strength, and used his hypnotic power on Spider-Woman. The Needle prepared to sew Spider-Woman's mouth shut, but was shocked to find that, just as he was nearly immune to her power, she was nearly immune to his for the same reason. Spider-Woman fired another venom blast at him, this time at point-blank range, which stunned the Needle long enough to be captured. The police arrested the Needle as Spider-Woman left. However, this encounter damaged Spider-Woman's romantic relationship with Hunt, as he was disappointed that he had been unable to help, when a few months earlier he had been useful against Pyrotechnics. In later encounters where Hunt was similarly more of a hindrance than a help, he reminisced about his failed confrontation with the Needle. The Needle was later captured by the Locksmith, a demented escape artist who intended to capture all superhumans in the San Francisco area with the help of Ticktock, his strange sidekick who had precognitive powers. For three years, he often followed Spider-Woman's trail as it led him to one target after another. As a master illusionist, the Locksmith captured his victims using his tricks, and locked them in cells the Locksmith had specifically designed to hide the power of the specific prisoner. As the Needle's power depended on its gaze, the Locksmith blindfolded the Needle; and Ticktock's powers warned of any escape attempts. The Locksmith captured at least thirteen other superhumans or costumed adventurers, before ensnaring Spider-Woman herself, but Spider-Woman collaborated with other inmates such as Gypsy Moth, Shroud, Tigra, and Poltergeist, until she managed to break free and lead a mass escape. The Locksmith was defeated and Spider-Woman had him imprisoned by the authorities, along with Ticktock and several of the more dangerous inmates such as the Needle; though she did let go of those she believed she could trust. One of the Locksmith's former prisoners, the Shroud, was a crime fighter posing as a criminal gang leader The Shroud saw an opportunity in what happened and decided to recruit several of the Locksmith's other ex-prisoners into his Night Shift criminal gang, based in Los Angeles and operating primarily at night, hence the name. fields.personality: Clinically insane and full of rage, the Needle was a brutal and cruel enemy who didn't mind endangering even innocents to achieve his goals, as demonstrated when he took housekeeper Yolanda Russo hostage. In combat, he attacked brutally, sometimes even from behind, and with clearly murderous intent, and was brave enough to attack enemies more powerful than himself like Hellstrom. Early in his career, the Needle had been a vigilante who targeted young males like the ones who had attacked him, capping their age at thirty; but he was willing to attack women or older men if they threatened his crusade. He used his "evil eye" to paralyze his victims, and then sewed their mouths shut, in a manner that seemed related to his own muteness. The Needle had a set of small needles and thread for this task, separate from his personal giant needle-shaped weapon. The Hangman theorized that the Needle's motivation for sewing criminals' mouths shut was due to the Needle's exhibitionist tendencies. Since joining Night Shift, the Needle proved to be good at working in a group: He obeyed orders in combat, learned to harness the powers of his fellow members, and even developed friendships with them: When the Hangman attempted to choke the Misfit, the Needle went to the Misfit's aid (though the Hangman withdrew his noose before it was needed). The Needle didn't seem to care about the jokes and puns his allies made at his expense, and they knew of the Needle's past with sewing mouths shut. Even in relaxed situations, the Needle rarely let go of his needle, and sometimes even raised it in victory. It is unclear what the Needle's dementia is. The Needle appears to be mute, and his Night Shift allies identify him as such, but he has spoken occasionally and complained loudly when struck in combat. It is possible that the muteness is psychological. It also seems clear that the Needle does not miss his former life as a tailor: From the moment he was struck, he was struck by a scythe. when she adopted her identity as the Needle, she made it clear that she didn't care about losing her business.
fields.notes: Several sources say that the Needle is mute, including characters who describe him as such, but the Needle once spoke at a Night Shift meeting to say that the Misfit isn't even symmetrical (which is ironic, because Needle's costume isn't either), he also sang with his companions during a ritual to summon Satannish, and has complained when he took a hit in combat against Moon Knight. Although Needle's profile in says he uses "conventional means" for transportation, at the time he was getting around using the sewers of Los Angeles and Night Shift hearses; and possibly Dansen Macabre's teleportation of the Tower of Shadows. In Jerry Hunt's nightmare seen in , the Needle's mask does not have the opening that allows him to see his right eye. Although the Needle and Ticktock have not been seen again after their incineration, their other three allies who died have since reappeared (Dansen Macabre in and ; the Digger in and ; and Tatterdemalion in and ); the resurrections of these characters have not been explained.
fields.trivia: It is unknown how the Needle gained his powers originally; his power augmentation by Satannish is documented as is his zombification, but not the origin of his "evil eye".

josef skala.name: Josef Skala
josef skala.origin: and her partner are riding in the back of a prison transfer truck with a criminal named Brunt. Brunt is turning State's evidence against the Russian mafia and there are many interested parties whom would sooner see him dead than inside a courtroom. One of these people happens to be the Punisher. The Punisher forces the police van off the road, and opens up the back. Holding Sara and Gleason at gunpoint, he forces them to handcuff one another and brings them inside a nearby cabin. Sarah calls upon the power of the to free herself and attacks the Punisher. As the two fight one another, Brunt breaks free and leaps onto Sara. The Witchblade digs into Brunt's flesh, causing massive amounts of pain. Suddenly, Brunt's head explodes in a spray of blood, and Sara sees the Punisher standing behind the headless body holding a smoking shotgun. The two argue with one another about their respective missions, but ultimately they each go their separate ways.

joseph unwanted.name: Joseph (Unwanted)
joseph unwanted.origin: Joseph was one of the many members of the Unwanted, inmates of the Ravencroft Institute who were experimented on and turned into vampires by the Weapon Plus to produce super-soldiers to fight in World War II. Joseph and the other Unwanted were sealed away in a vault for decades in a hidden basement below Ravencroft and helped crimelord Wilson Fisk disposed of the bodies of people he killed. When Fisk planned to rebuild Ravencroft as a prison instead of a mental hospital, the Unwanted forced Fisk to free them and threatened to reveal their partnership with Fisk to the public. Fisk tried to have the Unwanted eliminated by sending a strike force of villains and armed guards, but Joseph used his telepathic powers to trick the strike force into attacking illusions while his fellow Unwanted invaded Ravencroft from its hidden basement. However, Fisk was able to resist Joseph's telepathic power and killed him by snapping his neck.
powers: Telepath: Joseph possesses telepathic power of unknown strength. What is known is that he can manipulate the minds of several people at once and trick them with a complicated illusion for a period of time.

joseph armstrong.origin: Joseph Armstrong was a worker in an experimental plastics lab - and an insatiable drunkard - who unwittingly downed a bottle of an experimental formula, mistaking it for an alcoholic beverage. He gained superhuman elastic abilities from this act, but given his addiction-addled state they frequently manifested themselves in less-than-useful ways such as Armstrong inadvertently tying himself up like a pretzel. He was one of the four superhumans who answered Fight-Man's newspaper ad to join his nascent team, the Fight-Brigade, only for the team to break up in under six months due to Bigelow's stupidity. When the second Hooded Eye put a ten-million dollar price on Fight-Man's head, sending every villain in the city and many angry civilians after him, Fight-Man called the former Fight Brigade members for assistance. To avoid having to assist his obnoxious former partner, Armstrong lied to Fight-Man that he had lost his powers the previous week.

joseph bailey.name: Joseph Bailey
joseph bailey.origin: === Origin === Joey was the son of Paul Bailey and Sara Grey-Bailey, who was the elder sister of Jean Grey. Like his aunt, Joey was a mutant. === Nanny === When their house was blown up, Gailyn and Joey were kidnapped by Nanny, who brainwashed them with her "pixie dust" and forced them to forget about their parents. Gailyn and Joey were collectively codenamed Shatter-Box and joined the Lost Boys And Girls. === Living with Grandparents === They were rescued by Jean Grey and Cyclops, and then settled with their grandparents in Annandale-on-Hudson. Together with their grandparents, Gailyn and Joey were guests at the wedding of Jean and Cyclops. Some time later Jean and Scott visited the Grey's house, and Cyclops tried to check the children for mutant powers. This angered Jean, who wanted a happy childhood for the children. After it became clear that Sara died, Julia Grey and Brian Grey become guardians of Gailyn and Joey. During Operation: Zero Tolerance, Gailyn and Joey were hounded by the Prime Sentinels, but were saved thanks to Nate Grey and Roust. === Death === Joey was eventually killed, along with most members of the Greys, by the Shi'ar Death Commandos.
powers: He was stated to be an Epsilon-Beta Class mutant by the Prime Sentinels. It is not known what power he had, and whether he retained them after M-Day.

joseph browning.name: Joseph Browning
joseph browning.origin: Dr. Joseph Browning was a renowned psychiatrist. Businessman John Franks comes to him in excruciating pain and with the suggestion that he has a demon in his head. Dr. Browning confirmed that the idea of having a demon in his head was a fantasy due to a strong susceptibility to suggestion following association with an ignorant guide who made him believe it. After these words, the pain and the feeling of having a demon in his head disappeared from John and he left the doctor's office relieved, not imagining that the demon was real and had moved into Dr. Browning's head who began to have excruciating pain and suggestion of having a demon in his head.

joseph calhoun.name: Joseph Calhoun
joseph calhoun.origin: Joseph "Licorice" Calhoun is a mutant born in the early 20th century with reality-warping powers, who was rendered comatose by an assault. Many decades later, Licorice's mutant powers caused havoc as he began to wake from his comatose state. ===Before Coma=== Joseph's mutant powers manifested themselves at an early age, namely, his dreams are able to affect reality. That is, if he dreams about something, it happens in reality. As an adult, Joseph became a clarinet player in "Sweet" Tommy Connor's jazz Band in 1936 under the name "Licorice." The owner of the Flamingo Jazz Club, Mr. Cleveland, found out about Licorice's power and tried to use it benefit himself. He told Licorice that he had a horse running at Belmont and wanted Licorice to dream of a big win, but threatened to break Licorice's fingers if the horse did not win. The threat of violence frightened Licorice and he had awful violent dreams that night, which caused the horse's stable to burn down, killing the horse. The next day Mr. Cleveland sent some enforcers after Licorice. They found him and put him into an coma. ===Coma=== At some point S.H.I.E.L.D. found Licorice, and took him custody of him. Finally decades later, Licorice began to emerge from his coma and replayed the events of 1936 in his dream. As a result, New York City of the present was replaced with that of 1936. The Invisible Woman (Susan Storm), She-Hulk (Jennifer Walters), Human Torch (Jonathan Storm), and Nick Fury become trapped in the 1936 created by Licorice's mind and altered the events leading to his head injury. In particular, She-Hulk intervened and stopped Mr. Cleveland's enforcers from harming Licorice. From that point on, Licorice's mutant mind locked on to each member of the group. Consequently, Licorice's mind continued to alter reality across the globe as he accompanied them. For example, Nick Fury decided to travel to Germany to kill Hitler and thus prevent World War II, and as a result, Nick's mind was able to alter reality to recreate his idea of 1936. Nick seemingly killed Hitler, which was enough to cause things to snap back to reality. Eventually, the group was taken back to the S.H.I.E.L.D. headquarters where Licorice was being held in custody and Mister Fantastic (Reed Richards) explained the situation.

joseph cartelli.name: Joseph Cartelli
joseph cartelli.species: Human Mutate with genetic structure transformed by energies of force field generating belt.
joseph cartelli.origin: When Frank Cartelli was murdered, his son Joe vowed to avenge his father by waging war on crime. Acquiring a belt (from sources as yet unrevealed) that generated a force field, Joe fashioned an identity-concealing costume and went into action as the Blue Shield. In his civilian guise, he even worked his way into the crime syndicate, eventually becoming the assistant to the crime boss. He once had to help Alison Blaire (also known as the Dazzler) against the crime boss Bo Brannigan who was controlling the Terror Tank. After the battle, Alison Blaire told him she was to give a message to Joey from his mother and Joey later visited his mother in hospital. He later encountered Dazzler again when he interfered with an assassination attempt made at one of her concerts. Due to their proximity, the involved mobsters mistook Dazzler's road manager Lance as being the Blue Shield's secret identity, and the Shield and Dazzler had to team-up again to rescue him. thumb|left The Blue Shield's immediate activities afterwards are unknown, but he was next seen among the multitude of super-heroes and other super-powered beings kidnapped from Earth by Death and The Grandmaster. However, he was not among those few selected to take part in the two cosmic beings' "Contest of Champions", and was returned back to his world without much further ado. Joseph later attempted to join the Avengers, alongside Mechanaut, Speedball and Gladiatrix. When Captain America, who was trying them out for the team, was called away, Hydrobase, where the Avengers were then based, was visited by the Soviet Super Soldiers, who were considering defecting to the United States. Thinking the Soviets' appearance was a test, Joseph and the other auditionees attacked them, only to quickly lose the upper hand. Before they could be beaten, Captain America intervened and stopped the fight. Joseph and the other prospective Avengers were not offered membership. Joseph later became the head of security for Project Pegasus, and briefly resigned from the job after he failed to stop an alien threat from the Omnivore (Omnivore killed fifteen of Blue Shield's security staffers before being stopped by Quasar), before taking up the role again, in time to confront the fugitive Angler. After the Civil War, Joseph was considered as a potential recruit for the Initiative program. Having become a registered superhero, Blue Shield once tried to apprehend Spider-Man after spotting him while coming back from a bust. Since Spider-Man was teaming-up with registered hero Jackpot, Blue Shield had her help him stop Spider-Man. Blue Shield almost got to unmask Spider-Man, until Menace's presence distracted the heroes, giving Spider-Man a chance to slip away from Jackpot and Blue Shield's grasp. Following Hydra's sudden takeover of the United States of America under the leadership of an evil doppelganger of Captain America, Blue Shield joined the Underground, a contingent of America's remaining super heroes that fought against the new regime. Under the assumption that Captain America could have been mind-controlled, the Underground raided Doctor Faustus' institute. The mission failed, and among the assault's one hundred and sixteen casualties was Blue Shield.
